## What's new

- **Linux support.** KeepShot now ships for Linux x86_64 as an **AppImage**, a **.deb** and an **.rpm**, alongside the Windows installer. All formats update themselves from inside the app: the AppImage is replaced in place, and .deb/.rpm updates ask for your password. It needs a recent distribution (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40 or newer).
- **Wayland.** Captures go through the desktop's screenshot portal (GNOME may ask for permission the first time). Wayland does not let apps register global shortcuts, so bind `--capture` and `--history` as custom shortcuts in your desktop's keyboard settings; KeepShot's Settings shows the exact commands with a Copy button. On X11, shortcuts work as on Windows.
- **Command-line actions.** `keepshot --capture` and `keepshot --history` start a capture or open the history panel, on any platform.

> On GNOME, the tray icon needs the AppIndicator extension. If Print Screen is taken by the desktop's own screenshot tool, unbind it in the keyboard settings or pick another shortcut.

> The Windows installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher. Choose **More info → Run anyway**.
